STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: a round dinner plate is 25-28 cm; this one looks like a standard dinner plate, so about 26 cm.
b) Reference cue: cherry tomatoes (3 cm) are about 3 cm each. The plate spans roughly 9 tomato-lengths across the width (about 420 px at about 45 px per tomato), giving about 27 cm.
Both cues agree: width ≈ 26 cm. Area = 0.785 x 26^2 ≈ 530 cm².

- Cauliflower florets (white, top right): about 40 cm² footprint, thickness about 2 cm averaging 1 cm → 40 ml x 0.6 ≈ 25 g. Round to 30 g.
- Carrot pieces (orange, right and bottom): about 20% of plate, about 105 cm², thickness about 1 cm (one carrot slice thick, a few stacked at the thickest point, average ~1 cm) → 105 ml x 0.6 ≈ 65 g.
- Yellow squash/corn-like half (left, cut): about 9 cm diameter, about 2.5 cm thick, half-cylinder with a mound effect, footprint about 60 cm² x 2 cm x 0.5 ≈ 60 ml x 0.6 ≈ 40 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer; the food is a single layer, so nothing significant is hidden.

- Melon (cantaloupe): 34 kcal/100 g

Totals: about 150 + 50 + 30 + 65 + 40 = 335 g; energy ≈ 27 + 17 + 8 + 23 + 8 ≈ 83 kcal.
